item.title: The Camden Killer Who Was Nearly Stopped Before He Struck Again
item.description: Anthony Hardy was convicted of murdering three women in Camden, London, after the bodies of Elizabeth Valad and Bridgette MacClennan were discovered in rubbish bins near his home. Hardy had previously been investigated for violence against women and was released from psychiatric care shortly before two of the murders. He pleaded guilty and received three life sentences, later receiving a whole-life order in 2010.

item.title: The Disturbing Downfall Of Austin Harrouff
item.description: In August 2016, 19-year-old Austin Harrouff fatally attacked John Stevens and Michelle Mishcon Stevens at their Florida home and seriously injured a neighbor who tried to intervene. After years of psychiatric evaluations and delays, Harrouff was found not guilty by reason of insanity in 2022 and committed indefinitely to a secure mental health facility.

item.title: The Millionaire Accused Of Targeting Hundreds Of Women
item.description: Wealthy Japanese property developer Joji Obara was convicted of raping nine women and causing the death of Australian hostess Carita Ridgway. He was also convicted on appeal of abducting and dismembering British woman Lucie Blackman, whose remains were found in a seaside cave. Obara was sentenced to life in prison.

item.title: The Bever Brothers Who Murdered Their Entire Family
item.description: In 2015, brothers Robert and Michael Bever murdered their parents and three younger siblings inside their Broken Arrow, Oklahoma, home, while another sister survived the attack. Investigators uncovered evidence that the killings had been planned as the beginning of a much larger killing spree. Robert received consecutive life sentences without parole, while Michael was sentenced to consecutive life terms with parole eligibility only after 225 years.

item.title: The Disturbing Case Of Alyssa Bustamante
item.description: In 2009, 15-year-old Alyssa Bustamante was involved in the death of nine-year-old Elizabeth Olten in Missouri. Bustamante later pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and armed criminal action and received a life sentence with the possibility of parole, plus 30 years for the additional charge. The case drew widespread attention because of Bustamante's age and the circumstances surrounding the investigation.

item.title: Raoul Moat And The Seven Day Manhunt That Gripped Britain
item.description: In July 2010, Raoul Moat went on the run after shooting his ex-girlfriend Samantha Stobbart, killing her new partner Chris Brown, and seriously wounding police officer David Rathband. A huge armed operation followed across Northumberland, ending after a six-hour standoff in Rothbury when Moat died by suicide.
